doc.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: The Welk bubble machine
summary: How the bubble machine worked, taking it on the road, and Welk's golden touch.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: So how did they make the bubbles?

Well there was a bubble machine. As a matter of fact I always like to tell a joke with the audiences, that I don’t really play on the show, I just operate the bubble machine. But it was a circular wheel with holes, maybe five or six holes in this wheel. And the wheel would rotate down into a can with soapy water, and this wheel would just turn around and there was a fan that blowed through the holes and up into the air came the bubbles, behind the bandstand. And that was the first thing you would see on television, when the show started.
Did they take the bubble machine on the road?
We did have a traveling bubble machine, yes. And we all would hate that because it would get on our clothes and then on the horns.
Who would ever think of those little things you know?
Well I’ll tell you it seems like everything Mr. Welk did turned to gold. He was such a smart man and he knew exactly what the average public wanted to hear.
Yes, I know. People would make jokes about him you know, but as they say, he was laughing all the way to the bank I guess.
